state.goal: Fix demonstrated original PromptLab empty /catalogs HTTP400 at paged collection binding, preserving canonical permissions, current owner/store identity, signed continuations and existing single-owner hosts with smallest complete runtime change.
verified_facts: Compiler emits stable list occurrence correctly. State runtime queryPageRowsCanonical requires PageReadsBinding.scope {app,owner,ownerPackage}, sourceIdentity and optional cursor codec. worker/main.ts does not configure pageReads at all; only direct test hosts currently supply it.

AssemblyDeps.pageReads currently is one optional static binding. Assembly checks its app and owner equal appInfo.appId and current identity.team.team_id when ownerStorage exists. One assembled worker handles multiple configured physical owner D1 stores (local preview Cedar/Oak). Owner boundary resolves actual store once per read scope using current trusted Identity memberships, then final State reader rechecks authority and revision.

worker/main already validates declared app from checked compiled appDefinition, distinct configured owner/db routes, and constructs ownerStorage routing. It already configures canonical form signing from private CAN_FORM_BINDING_KEY; exact sourceFormRevision derives from checked artifact sources.

Existing createPageCursorCodec uses canonical 32byte private key, fixed HMAC domain can-page-cursor v2, 15-minute lease. Runtime binding digest adds app/owner/ownerPackage/sourceIdentity/model/current actor and team/compiler occurrence/State-owned queryDefinition. Current checks reject stale/tampered/cross-query/cross-actor cursor and retain original query time. A cursor never grants read authority.

The repair can use existing form private key with existing separate cursor MAC domain. It adds no user/source/URL-specified binding or secret option. A host without configured owner route/key must not gain a fabricated scope. Existing static bindings must remain supported.
state.acceptance: Actual installed empty and populated paged routes work for each configured owner, own next-page cursor works, cross-owner/actor/source misuse and wrong physical-store scope refuse, current authority/fence checks remain. No source rewrite, no weakening paged-host gate, no whole-worker rearchitecture unless needed.
state.tradeoff: All alternatives below must use the same verified owner routing and exact source identity, resolve only inside current read scope, retain public errors and existing static-host compatibility. Assess change size, correctness traceability, lifecycle cost and duplicated configuration fairly.

implementation.instructions: Select the best complete host-wiring approach for the verified multi-owner pagination failure, comparing implementation surface, secure store association and request lifecycle costs under the same acceptance.

criteria.trusted_factory: Extend existing AssemblyDeps.pageReads to accept its current static binding or a trusted host factory of admitted identity. Resolve factory exactly once after ownerStorage.forIdentity selects actual store, validate binding against declared app/selected team, and pass captured binding into the read scope. worker/main constructs it from existing checked app, owner routes, source revision and existing codec. Small union/callback seam; dynamic selection and order require direct tests, but no per-owner assembly or separate map carrier.
criteria.trusted_owner_map: Retain current static pageReads and add a trusted per-owner map of immutable PageReadsBinding entries, constructed by worker/main from its same configured routing list and shared codec/source revision. Assembly selects map entry only after actual owner store selection and validates scope. Explicit enumerable associations and no callback; new carrier/map selection path and coupling with owner route configuration must be maintained and bounded.
criteria.owner_specific_assembly: Keep AssemblyDeps.pageReads unchanged. Build/cache a separate assembly for each verified configured owner, with static binding and correct store, and route authenticated current-owner requests to that assembly after membership resolution. Static associations straightforward and no union/factory; changes worker lifecycle/request routing, duplicates or shares assembly preload/assets explicitly, and must preserve current access checks and cleanup.
